entry.title: THE LEANING OLD STUMP · CASE 001
entry.body: We used to dare each other to touch the Leaning Old Stump when we were kids. The dare was easy. It was the walk back nobody talked about.

entry.title: THE PINECONE · CASE 002
entry.body: Recovered near Cascade Pass, 1976. Bagged, tagged, photographed. Nothing about where it lay makes sense. The file stays open.

entry.title: THE WEATHERED FELLING AXE · CASE 003
entry.body: It was just sitting there, out past Rainier Foothills, like it had been left for someone to find. Maybe it was. Maybe that someone was me.

entry.title: THE CAMP TENT · CASE 004
entry.body: Let this entry attest that the article was found at Ape Canyon, untouched by weather in a season of storms. Philosophy offers no account of it.

entry.title: THE RAIN-SOAKED SPECIMEN JAR · CASE 005
entry.body: I found it half-covered near Cascade Pass. Nobody camps out there. Nobody has for years. I brought it back and I still wish I had not.

entry.title: BINOCULARS OF RAINIER FOOTHILLS · CASE 006
entry.body: Our party came upon the Binoculars of Rainier Foothills near Cascade Pass, abandoned in circumstances I hesitate to record. We carried it out; none among us would carry it twice.

entry.title: CANTEEN OF CEDAR HOLLOW · CASE 010
entry.body: We found the Canteen of Cedar Hollow on the second day. Whatever left it there had come back through the Logging Road that same night. The prints went right past our tent.

entry.title: THE FORGOTTEN SNOWCAPPED PEAK · CASE 011
entry.body: Everyone around Salmon Creek knows the Forgotten Snowcapped Peak. Nobody will give you directions to it. You find it, or it finds you.

entry.title: TRAIL SIGN OF RAINIER FOOTHILLS · CASE 012
entry.body: Item logged 1990. Chain of custody: incomplete. Explanation on file: none. Status: unresolved, like the rest of the drawer.

entry.title: THE BACKPACK · CASE 013

entry.title: LITTLE BROWN BAT OF SKOOKUM RIDGE · CASE 014
entry.body: A dark shape off Salmon Creek. Three witnesses, one photograph, no clear resolution. The report was filed and, per policy, quietly closed.

entry.title: THE SHY TOWNSEND CHIPMUNK · CASE 015
entry.body: I only saw it for a breath, out past Skookum Ridge. It watched me the way a person watches, then stepped back into the dark and was just gone.

entry.title: THE ANCIENT DUNGENESS CRAB · CASE 020
entry.body: We were near Cedar Hollow when the dogs quit barking all at once. That is when I saw it. I have not been back after dark since.

entry.title: RAVEN OF CEDAR HOLLOW · CASE 021
entry.body: Duration of sighting: under a minute. Location: Mist Basin. Conclusion: inconclusive, which is the only honest word for it.

entry.title: THE OLD-GROWTH SPOTTED OWL · CASE 024
entry.body: Second-hand account, Rainier Foothills, 1971. Consistent with prior The Old-Growth Spotted Owl reports — same height, same silence. Cross-reference earlier cases.

entry.title: THE SHY PILEATED WOODPECKER · CASE 026
entry.body: Our party, encamped near Cascade Pass in the autumn of 1971, observed a figure of uncommon stature. It regarded us without fear, then withdrew as though it had never been.

entry.title: THE MOSS-COVERED TOTEM POLE · CASE 027
entry.body: Locals will not camp within sight of the Moss-Covered Totem Pole. When asked why, they answer a different question. Noted, 1985; still unexplained.

entry.title: THE RIDGE WALKER · CASE 030
entry.body: The Ridge Walker was logged as driftwood. Driftwood does not leave that kind of track. The file remains, uncorrected, in the drawer marked open.

entry.title: THE BALD EAGLE · CASE 031
entry.body: Observed 1973 near Cascade Pass. Approximately human height, not human gait. No further comment was offered by the witness or requested of them.

entry.title: RACCOON OF SALMON CREEK · CASE 032
entry.body: Let the record show that on the road past Cedar Hollow, in the year 2010, a thing was seen which philosophy cannot yet explain.

entry.title: THE BOBCAT · CASE 033

entry.title: THE LEANING RANGER CABIN · CASE 034
entry.body: The Leaning Ranger Cabin appears in three surveys and is absent from four. All seven were conducted competently. No further survey is planned.

entry.title: THE MOSS-BACKED BLACK BEAR · CASE 035
entry.body: It was 1963 and I swore I would never tell anyone. But I know what stood at the edge of Salmon Creek, and it was no animal I can name.

entry.title: LOGGING TRUCK OF CASCADE PASS · CASE 036
entry.body: My uncle kept it in a drawer since 1990. Would not say where he got it. After he passed, I found the map it was wrapped in.

entry.title: BATSQUATCH OF CEDAR HOLLOW · CASE 050
entry.body: My grandfather saw it first. Now I have too, plain as day, out by the Logging Road. Whatever the Batsquatch of Cedar Hollow is, it remembers this valley.

entry.title: THE MOTHMAN · CASE 052
entry.body: Report from the Hoh Valley: a shape too large for any bear, moving without sound. No scat, no den. Witness sober. Logged as The Mothman.

entry.title: THE FOG-WRAPPED DOUGLAS FIR · CASE 058

entry.body: Found at Skookum Ridge. Standard recovery, non-standard circumstances. The report uses the word "placed" where "dropped" was expected.
